content.title: About
content.content: Reduced sodium mozzarella is a soft cheese made from cow’s milk with its salt level lowered to about 0.5 % compared to regular mozzarella. It retains the delicate flavor, elastic texture, and mild creaminess while providing significantly less sodium, making it suitable for those monitoring salt intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mozzarella originates from Italy, where it is often called the “queen of cheeses.”
The lower sodium content is achieved through specialized starter cultures and precise brining control.
The cheese melts beautifully, which is why it’s a favorite topping for pizza, salads, and pasta dishes.
Despite reduced salt, mozzarella remains a good source of protein and calcium.
Reduced sodium helps lower the risk of high blood pressure.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and tooth health and plays a role in muscle contraction and nerve signaling.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth, repair, and satiety.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt intake helps manage blood pressure and reduces kidney strain.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mozzarella provides vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fermentation introduces beneficial bacteria that can support gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience digestive discomfort after consuming cheese.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions to casein can occur in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Mozzarella contains saturated fats; moderate consumption is advised for low‑fat diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced sodium mozzarella can be sliced for salads, used as a pizza topping, added to pasta, baked in casseroles, or enjoyed as a snack. It pairs well with tomatoes, basil, olive oil, and fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. It stays fresh for up to 2 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour smell or an off‑texture.
